description: We are a multidisciplinary team passionate about applying Artificial Intelligence, Biomedical Engineering, and emerging technologies to solve challenges in space exploration and human health.
summary: AstroBone is health monitoring software for astronauts on long missions, where a message to Earth can take 22 minutes and no doctor is on board. A 5-minute daily self-check gathers health indicators on the device itself: a camera knee-movement test, a 3-minute reaction test (PVT-B), camera pulse, sleep, mood, symptoms, vital signs and radiation dose. Each reading is compared with the astronaut's own baseline, poor captures are refused and repeated, and the app gives a safe next step: re-check, tell the medical officer today, or contact them now, plus a short report for the flight surgeon. NASA OSDR and DONKI data decide what the check asks for and when; a 3D digital twin shows the result on the body; it runs in the browser, works offline and no health data leaves the device.https://youtu.be/tLVDlBOgUGc

Live app: https://mysunatislam.github.io/astrobone-space-apps-2026/

Code: https://github.com/mysunatislam/astrobone-space-apps-2026

30-second demo: https://youtu.be/tLVDlBOgUGc

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

On the way to Mars, a message to Earth can take up to 22 minutes one way, and there is no flight surgeon on board. AstroBone lets astronauts gather their own health indicators, then evaluate and act on them.

- Gather: a 5-minute daily self-check on a laptop or phone. The camera measures knee extension (MediaPipe pose on the device plus our own hybrid knee model) and resting pulse. A 3-minute reaction test (PVT-B) measures alertness. The astronaut adds sleep, fatigue, mood, stress, immune symptoms, blood pressure, blood sugar, temperature, oxygen and radiation dose (Bluetooth cuffs, oximeters and thermometers can be read in). A Crewmate check covers a crewmate with sudden chest pain.

- Evaluate: a poor capture is refused and repeated, never reported as a decline. Each reading is compared with the astronaut's own baseline: one value just outside the usual range asks for a re-check; two in a row, or one far outside, is logged for review (a lab quality-control multirule). A drift rule (CUSUM) catches slow loss. Fixed safety limits from public guidance (AHA, ADA, Mayo Clinic, NHS) apply from day one.

- Act: a clear next step with a due time (re-check in 24 h, tell the medical officer today, or contact them now), worded for where the crew is, plus a 1.6 kB plain-text report for the flight surgeon that fits a slow deep-space link. A 3D digital twin lights up the body systems that changed. It never diagnoses or prescribes.

NASA DATA DOES REAL WORK

- OSD-804: bone loss above the knee after 37 days in space, so the knee test comes first every day.

- OSD-656 and OSD-569: an Inspiration4 immune marker stayed raised 45 days after return, so the immune checklist runs daily for 45 days after any landing.

- We replayed our own rules, unchanged, on the four Inspiration4 crew members' real blood results (OSD-569, OSD-575): mean cell volume fell in all four the day after landing, and the data set our blood-sugar alarm level.

- OSDR ISS dosimeters (0.20-0.35 mGy/day), Curiosity's Mars-cruise dose (0.46 mGy/day) and 40 real solar particle events from NASA DONKI frame the radiation log. NASA's 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight are mapped to the indicators that watch for them.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

The astronaut notices a change at the next daily check, not at the next ground contact. Nothing needs a network: it works fully offline and health data never leaves the device. On Earth, the same app can serve rural clinics in Bangladesh, where a doctor is also far away.

HOW WE CHECKED IT

- Knee, REHAB24-6 (9 adults, lab motion capture): error per repetition 21.7 -> 13.2 degrees, better for all 9 people the model never saw.

- Camera pulse, MCD-rPPG (40 people, finger sensor): 2.1 bpm average error.

- False alarms, simulation of 1,000 healthy astronauts x 60 days: 44.8 % of healthy days flagged by a one-value rule, 11.4 % by ours, while a 10-degree knee loss is still caught within 14 checks in 98 % of runs.

- 521 automated tests and a clean WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility scan.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Real NASA crew data is used to test the app's own rules, not only shown as charts. The app refuses bad data instead of reporting it. A 3D twin turns numbers into a body the astronaut can read at a glance.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Privacy (on-device only, optional AES-256 encryption), no connection to Earth, false alarms that wear out trust, colour-blind-safe statuses, and safety: it never names a condition. Limits: the demo astronaut Elena Torres is synthetic; the NASA cohorts are mice and a four-person, three-day flight, so they set what to watch, never a personal threshold; the seated knee test is not yet compared with a goniometer; no astronaut study has been run. It is a research prototype, not a medical device.

TOOLS WE USED

JavaScript, Vite, three.js, a service worker for offline use, Python for the NASA data scripts, Google MediaPipe, ME-rPPG and Silero VAD (on-device AI), onnxruntime-web, Z-Anatomy 3D anatomy. AstroBone builds on our own earlier open-source work; the full commit history is public.

USE OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI)

SI tools used: Claude Code (Anthropic) for most of the code and tests, the NASA data scripts, the simulations, validation, documentation and video editing; OpenAI Codex for the breathing module, interface changes and tests; DeepFilterNet3 and RNNoise to remove noise from our own voice recordings. They worked on public NASA files, public research datasets, synthetic demo astronauts and our own voice; no real person's health data. No SI-generated images, video or voice are in our videos. The team set the direction, reviewed every change and is responsible for every claim. Details: https://github.com/mysunatislam/astrobone-space-apps-2026/blob/main/AI_USE_DISCLOSURE.md

NEXT

A goniometer study of the seated knee test (already built into the app), a pilot in an analog mission habitat, and real crew records through NASA's data access process.
